text: More than 2,400 years ago, a man named Siddhartha Gautama lived and taught in north-east India.
According to tradition, he sat in meditation under a fig tree at Bodh Gaya and became the Buddha, “the awakened one”.
src: Siddhartha Gautama / he lived and taught in the Ganges plain of north-east India / in north-east India in the 5th century BCE
The traditional account tells how / Seated in meditation beneath a fig tree at Bodh Gaya, he attained awakening and became the Buddha, the “awakened one”

text: Buddhists believe that suffering comes from craving, which means wanting things too much.
They follow a path of good actions, meditation and wisdom to end it.
src: a path of ethics, meditation and insight leads to its end

text: Monks and nuns gave up their homes and lived on gifts of food from others.
Great monasteries such as Nalanda drew students from all over Asia.
src: Monks and nuns gave up property and family life / depended on alms; lay followers gave food
centres such as Nalanda attracted students from across Asia

text: Kings, monks and merchants carried Buddhism across Asia, to China, Korea, Japan, Tibet and beyond.
In Java, the great temple of Borobudur was built.
src: Carried across Asia by kings, monks and merchants / carried it to Sri Lanka, Central Asia, China, Korea, Japan, Tibet and Southeast Asia

text: In Korea, Buddhist holy writings were carved on more than 80,000 wooden blocks.
The oldest printed book that has a date is a Buddhist scripture from China.
src: the Korean Tripitaka Koreana, carved on more than 80,000 wooden blocks in the 13th century
